steps.name: Load counts, QC, TMM normalization
steps.context: Human liver bulk RNA-seq, raw integer salmon counts, gene symbols as identifiers. 2 samples total: 1 treated, 1 control. No replication anywhere, so no dispersion estimation is possible in this or any downstream step.
steps.question: Are the 2 liver samples (treated vs control, per metadata.csv condition column) usable as-is — library sizes, gene detection, and what TMM normalization factors and logCPM values do they yield?
constraints: Do not attempt dispersion estimation or任何 model-based p-values in this step
Do not impute or fabricate a second sample per condition
Gene identifiers are HGNC-style symbols; do not re-map them in this step
steps.description: Read /eval-four-models-without-no-replicates-1v1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 gene symbols x 2 sample columns; the 3rd column in the profile is the gene-symbol index) and metadata.csv (2 rows, condition column). Verify sample names in the count matrix match the metadata rows exactly; stop with a clear error if not, and use the condition values as found in the file to label treated vs control. Compute per-sample library sizes, total counts, detected-gene counts (CPM > 1) and top-expressed genes as QC. Filter low-expression genes (keep genes with CPM > 1 in at least one sample — note with 2 samples this is the only sensible rule) and report how many of the 12000 genes survive. Apply edgeR TMM normalization, output the filtered DGEList-equivalent matrix, TMM factors, and a logCPM matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Sample names in counts.csv columns match metadata.csv rows 1:1, or the mismatch is reported as a blocker
Per-sample QC table written (library size, detected genes, TMM factor, percent top-100 CPM)
Filtered gene count reported out of 12000
Normalized logCPM matrix written as CSV

steps.name: DE under assumed BCV + sensitivity grid
caveats: With 2 samples, edgeR cannot estimate a common, trended, or tagwise dispersion; dispersion must be set explicitly, not estimated
FDR over 12k genes under an assumed BCV will be anti-conservative; the consistent-hits list is the deliverable, not any single scenario's FDR column
steps.context: Continues from T1S1's filtered TMM-normalized matrix. This is the dataset's central limitation: 1 treated vs 1 control means dispersion is a prior, not an estimate. The BCV sensitivity grid is the plan's honesty mechanism — calls that vanish at BCV 0.4 or 1.0 are fold-change observations, not findings.
steps.question: Which genes show the largest and most consistent treated-vs-control fold changes in the liver samples, and which of those calls survive stronger assumed biological variability (BCV 0.1 vs 0.4 vs 1.0)?
steps.description: Using the T1S1 filtered, TMM-normalized object, run edgeR exactTest for treated vs control three times with dispersion fixed to the edgeR case-study priors: BCV 0.1 (same tissue), 0.4 (between human tissues / strong biological heterogeneity), 1.0 (conservative). Per the edgeR framework (McCarthy, Chen & Smyth 2012, NAR) these p-values are conditional on the assumed BCV and carry no true error-rate guarantee with n=1 per group — the step must state this in its outputs, not bury it. Produce: (1) a full gene-level table — gene symbol, log2FC, logCPM, and the p/FDR under each BCV scenario; (2) a short 'consistent hits' list: genes with |log2FC| >= 1 that remain nominally significant (FDR < 0.05 under the assumed BCV) at BCV 0.1 AND 0.4, annotated with which drop out at 1.0; (3) the same ranking expressed as an ordered log2FC list (no threshold) to feed T1S3. Report counts of up- vs down-regulated genes per scenario.
acceptance_criteria: Three BCV scenarios each produce a full 12k-gene result table
Consistent-hits list with |log2FC| >= 1 and FDR < 0.05 under both BCV 0.1 and 0.4, with survival at BCV 1.0 annotated
Ordered log2FC ranking of all filtered genes written for downstream use
Output explicitly states p-values are conditional on the assumed BCV and are not valid inference

steps.name: WikiPathways enrichment on log2FC ranking
caveats: fgsea minSize/maxSize defaults will drop tiny and huge pathways — report how many of the collection's pathways entered the test
Gene sets whose members mostly failed the T1S1 expression filter are tested on shrunken rankings; report the effective set sizes
steps.context: Input is a ranked gene list from T1S2, not a hit list, because with no replication a thresholded hit list is arbitrary while the full ranking carries all the data. Reference data needed: human pathway gene sets in GMT form with HGNC symbols (WikiPathways 2026.07.10 human collection is staged in the reference store).
steps.question: Is the treated-vs-control liver expression shift concentrated in recognizable biological pathways, rather than scattered across genes?
steps.description: Run fgsea preranked GSEA using the T1S2 all-gene log2FC ranking (decreasing |none| tie handling) against the human WikiPathways gene set collection staged in the reference store (GMT: one pathway per line, '%'-delimited descriptor, HGNC member symbols — identifier space matches this dataset's gene symbols directly; confirm overlap between ranking genes and GMT members and report the matched-set statistics). Report per-pathway NES, nominal p, and BH-adjusted p, plus leading-edge gene sets for the top pathways. If the reference GMT is absent from the environment, fall back to a plain over-representation test on the T1S2 consistent-hits list using clusterProfiler's built-in universe handling and say which analysis ran.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full filtered log2FC ranking with GMT-overlap stats reported (pathways used / dropped for size)
Table of pathways by adjusted p with NES and direction (up in treated vs up in control)
Leading-edge genes extracted for the top 10 pathways
Output states that with n=1 per group the ranking is a fold-change ordering and enrichment is exploratory

plan.title: Treated vs control liver DE, 1v1 no-replicate design
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw salmon gene-level counts for 12000 human liver genes across exactly 2 samples — 1 treated and 1 control (metadata.csv is 2x2), with no biological replication. With n=1 per group, dispersion cannot be estimated and no method can produce statistically valid p-values; the honest design is (a) a standard TMM-normalized edgeR pipeline for fold changes and expression quantification, (b) an exact test run under an explicitly assumed biological coefficient of variation (BCV), repeated across a sensitivity grid (BCV 0.1 / 0.4 / 1.0 per the edgeR case-study guidance) so the user sees which genes' calls survive stronger variance assumptions, and (c) a rank-based pathway analysis (fgsea on the log2FC ranking against the human WikiPathways GMT staged in the reference store), which is the standard replication-free way to ask whether the observed shift is structured rather than gene-by-gene. All inferential outputs are labelled exploratory: the fold-change ordering is data-driven, the p-values are assumption-dependent, and nothing here supports an error-rate claim.
